spans.s: भम्भ भम्भ, अस्, m. smoke; a fly.
भम्भरालिका, f. a gnat, musquito, gad-fly.

भम्भारव भम्भा-रव, अस्, m. (onomato-
poetic), the lowing of a cow; (also बम्भा-रव.)

भम्भासार भम्भासार, अस्, m., N. of a
king of Magadha.

1. भाम, अस्, m. (for 2. see rt. भाम्, p. 706),
light, brightness, splendor; the sun.
—भाम-नी, ईस्,
ईस्, इ, Ved. ‘bearing light,’ an epithet of Puruṣa.

2. भाम, अस्, m. (for 1. see p. 704, col. 2; for
3. see below), passion, wrath, fury, anger; (आ), f. a
passionate woman; = सत्य-भामा, one of the
wives of Kṛṣṇa.

भाम 3. भाम or भामक, अस्, m. a sister's
husband.

1. भामिन्, ई, इनी, इ (fr. 1. भाम; for 2. see
under rt. भाम्), shining, glittering, beautiful, hand-
some; proud; (इनी), f. a handsome woman; N. of
the daughter of a Gandharva.
—भामिनी-विलास, अस्,
m., N. of a poem by Jagan-nātha in four chapters,
(the first book contains allegorical precepts, the
second includes amatory subjects, the third an elegy
[karuṇa] on the death of a wife, the fourth teaches
that consolation is only to be obtained by adoration
of Kṛṣṇa.)

2. भामिन्, ई, इनी, इ (for 1. see p. 704, col. 2),
passionate, angry; (इनी), f. an angry or passionate
woman, vixen, (often used as a term of endearment,
in the same sense as मानिनी.)

भाम् भाम्, cl. 1. A. भामते, बभामे,
&c., or (by Dhātu-pāṭha

) cl.
10. P. भामयति, &c., Ved. to be angry or wrath-
ful; to be impatient: Intens. बाभाम्यते, to be
very angry.
भामित, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. enraged, angry.

भामह भामह, अस्, m., N. of the author
of the Mano-ramā commentary and of a treatise on
the art of rhetoric.
